text:
maria_support: Customer (Acct 8243) can't SSO into prod since yesterday after IdP cert rotation. They get an error page that says "InvalidDestination" from our SP. They can auth into other apps fine. Ticket: https://support.redwood-inference.com/t/3245

alex_infra: I reproduced quickly. IdP sends SAMLResponse where Destination includes query params and a fragment, e.g. https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs?env=prod#_=_ . Our SP metadata has ACS URL without query/fragment.

olivia_eng: logs show Recipient check failed: expected "https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs" got "https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs?env=prod#_=_". This is strict equality check in saml_processor.validate_destination().

maria_support: Customer says they didn't change IdP config beyond rotating cert. IdP team says some providers append tracking params automatically during rotation flows. So this only surfaced now.

luis_saml: quick note: SAML spec allows Destination to include query; Destination check should be exact per some libs but most SPs tolerate query/fragment normalization. We need to decide: fix parsing to normalize URL (strip fragment, ignore query order) or ask customers to update metadata.

alex_infra: For quick triage I posted a curl with SAMLResponse from the customer (sanitized). Repro command:

```
curl -X POST 'https://app.redwood.com/saml/acs?env=prod#_=_' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -d 'SAMLResponse=<base64>' -d 'RelayState=abc'
```

Response: 400 InvalidDestination. Stack:
```
File "saml_processor.py", line 412, in validate_destination
  if dest != metadata_acs:
ValueError: RecipientMismatch
```

maria_support: Customer asked for workaround while you fix it. Any temporary option?

luis_saml: Workaround: In the IdP, configure the ACS to match SP exactly (remove query/fragment) OR update SP metadata to add ACS with expected query param (not ideal). We can also add a service-side lenient check for a short-term fix.

olivia_eng: I'm going to draft a 1-line change to normalize Destination by stripping fragment and normalizing query param ordering before equality check. Quick unit tests pass locally.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: eng-deploy pipeline #4245 -> staging at 2026-03-16T18:12:00Z, canary to prod after smoke.

alex_infra: can you also add a feature flag to keep strict behavior by default? We need to avoid regressions for customers relying on exact check.

luis_saml: yes, feature flag "saml.accept_normalized_destination" default false. We'll enable for this customer only in tenant config. Patch ready: PR #7892.

maria_support: Great. Tell the customer we have a tenant-level flag and a short-term patch; ETA for canary to prod?

olivia_eng: Canary started 18:20Z, smoke passed. Enabling feature flag for tenant 8243 now.

alex_infra: Flag enabled for tenant 8243. I tested with their SAMLResponse curl, got 200 and user redirected to app.

maria_support: Customer confirmed SSO works now. They thanked us. I'll keep ticket open until prod deploy completes.

luis_saml: Plan: follow-up to harden SAML parser, add canonicalization step and robust unit tests covering query ordering and fragments. We'll roll into next release.

maria_support: Closing loop here — set ticket status to pending-customer-confirmation and note mitigation applied. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Production deploy #4245 completed at 2026-03-16T19:03:12Z, rolled back 0 hosts.

maria_support: Thanks team. Logging postmortem notes in support ticket and will coordinate with product if we should flip default flag globally.
